subject.title: fix(wechat): preserve existing accounts across hot reload

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `reload.accountIndexReloadPaths` as a supported channel-plugin contract for externally managed account indexes, with this WeChat behavior merged after live proof or an explicit gateway-owner waiver?
rationale: The core implementation is a new plugin-facing lifecycle capability rather than a local WeChat-only repair, so maintainers must choose the permanent compatibility and validation standard.

options.title: Approve the generic contract with exact-head proof
options.body: Accept the metadata capability, require redacted live WeChat A+B evidence on the final head or explicitly waive it, and retain the marker-only safeguards.

options.title: Keep the behavior owner-local
options.body: Do not add the generic metadata contract; require the Weixin plugin and its release process to own any account-index handoff through an existing supported seam.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic contract with exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Accept the metadata capability, require redacted live WeChat A+B evidence on the final head or explicitly waive it, and retain the marker-only safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged account-scoped reload work is the closest current-main precedent for the Gateway lifecycle and plugin capability boundary.
